biography: Felipe Fraga emerged from the vibrant karting scene of Brazil, a whirlwind of raw talent and untamed aggression. His father, a local mechanic, fueled his early passion, spending countless nights tuning his son's kart in their small garage. A defining moment came at the 2014 Brazilian Karting Championship where, despite starting last after a mechanical failure, Fraga stormed through the field to win, showcasing his relentless determination. Transitioning to GT racing, he quickly made a name for himself with blistering pace and daring overtakes, earning him a spot with Mercedes-AMG. Currently, Fraga balances his commitments in IMSA with Oreca 07 #74 and various GT programs, still striving for that elusive overall championship title.
drivingStyle: Fraga is known for his aggressive, high-risk driving style. He attacks corners with maximum commitment, often pushing the limits of grip and occasionally exceeding them. While his raw speed is undeniable, his tire management can be inconsistent, sometimes leading to late-race struggles. He thrives under pressure, often delivering his best performances when the stakes are highest, but his tendency to overdrive can also lead to costly mistakes.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry from their karting days, Rossi's clinical precision clashed with Fraga's aggressive style, often resulting in on-track clashes.
Dubois, a veteran GT driver, publicly criticized Fraga's driving as reckless, sparking a heated exchange in the media and intensifying their on-track battles.
Both Brazilians competing in international series, their rivalry is fueled by national pride and the desire to be recognized as the top Brazilian driver.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks, inherited from his grandfather, for every race.
Listens to a specific Brazilian samba song on repeat for the hour leading up to the race start.
Visits the trackside coffee stand and orders a double espresso exactly 30 minutes before qualifying, without fail.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about speed; it's about heart. You have to be willing to risk everything to win."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2016 Stock Car Brasil championship after a season-long battle, securing the title with a dramatic last-lap overtake in the final race.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final hour of the 24 Hours of Daytona while driving for AMR, costing his team a likely victory and attracting heavy criticism from the team owner.
